title: Every item gets its own page
text: Tap anything in Inventory to open its page: a big photo, how much is left (drag the slider), its dates, what you paid and the best price seen, when you bought it before, and the recipes that use it. Up top: Used some, Finish, Spoiled (counted as waste) and Restock (back on the list, with the store you usually buy it at). Move, edit details, set dates or delete (with Undo) are under ⋯.

title: Fits every screen better
text: On a computer, pages use the full width (Home gets two columns, Recipes up to six cards a row, Inventory two columns) and Settings has its sections on the left. Tablets get a compact side rail. What can I make? is in the sidebar, pages show a quick outline while they load, the update notice is readable in dark mode, and the red dot on Settings now means an update you haven't seen. On a computer, press / to search, N to add to the list, or G then H, R, P, S or I to switch tabs (Settings → Help lists them).

title: Find recipes for what I have
text: Ideas now only shows real, published recipes. With an OpenAI key, AI searches recipe sites using everything in your inventory (what's expiring first); TablePlan then opens each page, reads the site's own recipe and checks it against your kitchen. Results from TheMealDB, Spoonacular and the open-source Wikibooks Cookbook are mixed into one list, fewest missing first, each showing where it's from. Recipes saved earlier from AI ideas are kept; Settings → Recipe ideas lets you review them.

title: One place for what needs using
text: Tap Expiring on Inventory (or the expiring soon tile on Home) to see what's Expired, what to Use soon (3 days or less) and what's gone Stale (not touched in 3 weeks, freezer aside). Each item has one-tap answers: Used, Gone (counted as waste in Spending), Still good, and Find recipes, which opens Use it up for just that food.

title: A faster view for big stock-ups
text: While scanning, tap Batch at the top of the scan bar for one dense list in large type: name, place, count, a How full chip (tap to cycle) and a date chip. A summary stays pinned on top, like “14 items scanned · 2 to review”. Swipe a row left to remove it. Tap Cards to switch back; TablePlan remembers your choice.

title: Slide to say how much is left
text: Open an inventory item and drag the slider on its photo (or across the card) to show how much is left. It snaps to Empty, ¼, ½, ¾ and Full, updates the amount from the package size, and Undo is one tap. Slide it to empty and TablePlan offers to put it back on your list.

title: Product photos that look the part
text: Inventory tiles show each product's photo on a neutral rounded square, so mixed photos look tidy. Open an item to add or change its photo, or tap Cut out background: it's done on your device, you can fix the edges with a brush, and Use original photo puts it back any time.

title: Browse groceries by picture
text: Shopping → Browse common items is now a picture grid by aisle. Each aisle and item shows what's already at home ("1 at home · ½ left"), so you don't buy twice. Tap to pick, long-press to choose how many.

title: A quicker start and a quick tour
text: First-time setup is down to your account, your household and stores (Aldi and Costco to start, change them as you like), plus optional AI and notifications; the rest waits in the Getting started checklist. Then a one-minute tour points out Home, Plan, Recipes, What can I make?, Shopping, Inventory and Settings. Skip it or snooze it for a week, and replay it from Settings → Help. New here? Explore with sample recipes, and wipe them any time.

title: Heads-up when a meal is missing something
text: Home now shows up to two of today's and tomorrow's meals that are still missing ingredients, counted from what's really set aside for each meal (food reserved for another meal, expired food and unknown scans don't count). Turn on Settings → Day-before heads-up and Morning check to get a message 24 hours before you start cooking and on the morning itself.

title: The right pan when you scale
text: Recipes now know their pan (9×13, 9 inch round, 12-cup muffin tin…). Scale a bake and TablePlan asks: keep your pan (it'll be deeper, so bake longer), use a different pan (it suggests one that fits), or doesn't matter. It remembers your answer for that recipe. Add the pans you own in Settings → Pans I have, and scanned recipes that don't say a size ask "What size pan?" in the quick look.

title: Faster shopping lists
text: Start typing and TablePlan suggests what you've bought before, your foods and about 300 common groceries ("2 milk" works too). Tap your usual items, or browse common items by aisle. When you scan or log a receipt, the generic "Milk" on your list is matched to what you actually bought, and you're asked when it's not clear. Next time you add it, the list shows what you bought last time and where.

title: Recipe ideas from your kitchen
text: What can I make? has an Ideas tab (or tap Cook with what I have): published recipes from TheMealDB, the Wikibooks Cookbook and Spoonacular (if you add a key), ranked by what you already have. Preview one, import it, plan it, or add what's missing to your list. Plus: Inventory ⋯ → Export gives a CSV or a copy-paste list, for everything or just what you've selected.

title: Better recipe photos
text: Tap a recipe's photo to choose from up to six: the recipe's own page first, then openly licensed photos (and Unsplash or Pexels if you add a key). Crop to 4:3, square or 16:9; location and camera details are removed. With AI you can create a photo or enhance yours, compare them side by side, and go back to your original any time. AI photos are labelled.

title: Kitchen check-in
text: Once a week (Sunday evening by default, or every 2 weeks, or off), TablePlan asks about the handful of items it's least sure of: past their date, opened a while ago, untouched for weeks, nearly finished, or bought so regularly they're probably gone. Swipe right for still have, left for gone, or tap Running low; Undo fixes a slip, and All good skips the rest. It learns how fast your household goes through things.

title: Budget and prices
text: Set a weekly or monthly grocery budget (split by store if you like) and Home shows how it's going, with a heads-up at 80% and 100%. Recipes show what they cost per serving, the list shows prices and totals per store, the plan shows the week's cost, and Almost there shows what it takes to finish a recipe. Prices come from your receipts first, then prices you set, Kroger, web estimates with their source page, and US averages. ≈ marks an estimate, and nothing is ever guessed. Spending breaks it down by week, store and category, and shows what was thrown away.

title: What can I make?
text: Recipes → What can I make? checks every recipe against your inventory: Make now (everything's here), Almost there (1–3 things missing, added to your list in one tap) and Use it up (recipes for food expiring in the next 3 days). Expiring ingredients are marked wherever ingredients show, Home counts what's expiring soon, and with AI you can search the web for more recipes. Every link is opened and checked first, and importing still spots duplicates.

title: Scanning never gets stuck
text: Scan as fast as you like: every code is handled in order, double reads are ignored, and a barcode nobody knows goes straight in as “Unknown item” to review later, with no typing mid-scan. Add details when it suits you: photograph the package, type a name, add a product photo. TablePlan remembers it for next time (only in your household). Misreads are caught, and Settings → Test barcode lookup shows what each database says.

title: Cooked by mistake? Undo it
text: Every “cooked” can be undone and puts the ingredients back exactly. On the plan, ✓ Cook now needs a second tap, and a cooked meal's ⋯ menu has “Not cooked yet”. Diary entries can be edited or deleted.

title: Scan recipes back to back
text: Point your camera at a cookbook page: it snaps when the page is sharp and steady. Add more pages, tap Done and start the next recipe while TablePlan reads the last one. Anything unclear (a missing title, an amount, a cut-off step, a recipe you already have) waits for a quick look.

title: Pick your look
text: A cleaner black-and-white design is the new default. Prefer color? Choose Midnight, Blossom or Forest, in light or dark, under Settings → Appearance.

title: Everyone gets their own sign-in
text: Each person in your household signs in as themselves with a password or PIN and shares the same recipes, plans and lists. Admins add people in Settings → Members.

title: Getting started checklist
text: A short checklist on Home ticks itself off as you set things up. Rename, hide or add your own steps, and hide the card when you're done.

title: How long it really takes
text: Every recipe shows a start-to-finish time and how much of it is hands-on. Tap it for the breakdown. Your plan says when to start cooking to eat on time, and TablePlan learns your pace from cook mode.

title: Timers in cook mode
text: Every time a recipe states becomes a timer. Run several at once: they keep counting between steps and after a reload, and they beep, buzz and show a banner when time's up. Start cooking also opens right away now.

title: A fresh green look
text: TablePlan has a new green look with clearer type. Pick Light, Dark or System in Settings, under Appearance.

title: Fits your iPhone better
text: From the Home Screen, buttons now sit below the status bar and Dynamic Island, and typing no longer zooms the page.

title: Start a section over
text: Settings → Danger zone resets your inventory, recipes, plan, list, trips or diary, always after saving a backup first.

title: Select several in Inventory
text: Tap Select to move, use up, date or delete many items at once, with Undo.

title: Cooking diary
text: Every meal you cook is saved with your stars, a note and a photo, and your favorites come up more often in plans.

title: Make it my way
text: Ask for a recipe spicier, dairy-free or faster, see exactly what changes, and keep it as your own version.

title: Use-by dates you can trust
text: Use-by dates you can trust: only printed dates you enter, or a countdown once opened.

title: How full, and when it's due
text: When you stock up, tap ½ or ¼ for things already open, and add the printed date in one tap.

title: A fresh look
text: Recipes open on a big plate photo with a cleaner ingredient list, and Home now shows just your list, your week and tonight's dinner.

title: A list that knows what you have
text: What's already in your inventory is set aside for your next meals, so the list only shows what you still need, tagged with the meals that need it.

title: Always have
text: Mark basics like salt or oil as “Always have” and they'll never land on your list again.

title: Log a grocery trip
text: Snap your receipt or scan what you bought: list items get ticked off, your inventory fills up, and prices are saved by store.

title: More than one meal a day
text: Plan breakfast, lunch, sides and dessert too: tap + on any day, and pick the meal at the top of the recipe picker.

title: Inventory, with a grid view
text: The Pantry tab is now Inventory, with a slot grid that shows how much is left and what to use first.

title: Stock up your way
text: Choose scanner, camera or type it in, and pick the fridge, freezer or pantry before you start.

title: Barcode scanning
text: Scan with your camera or a USB/Bluetooth scanner: each item lands in your inventory with its size and brand, and gets ticked off your list.

title: Produce stickers and store brands
text: Type the number on a fruit sticker (4011 is bananas), and store brands like Great Value or Kirkland match the right food.

title: One name per food
text: Recipes, your list and your inventory now agree on what each food is, and you can merge duplicates in Settings → Foods.

title: Cleaner recipes
text: Recipe names use proper title case, and ingredients show the food first with the amount underneath, even for a pinch or “to taste”.

title: Reword with AI
text: Make a recipe's steps clearer in one tap, without changing amounts, and switch back to the original whenever you like.

title: Recipe categories
text: Sort recipes into categories like Main dish or Soup, filter by them, and set them for many recipes at once.

title: Select several recipes
text: Tap Select on the Recipes tab to delete or categorize many recipes at once.

title: Mark as cooked
text: Tick off a meal from the recipe page or the end of cook mode, and the ingredients come out of your inventory.

title: Always up to date
text: When TablePlan is updated, your phone picks up the new version on its own.

title: Arrange with AI
text: Pick several recipes and let TablePlan spread them across your empty days, with quick meals on weeknights.

title: Plan one day at a time
text: “Plan my 2 weeks” walks you through each empty day and shows recipes that aren't on the plan yet.

title: Ticked items stay put
text: Items you tick off stay on the list, crossed out, for a few hours, so a mis-tap is easy to undo.

title: Amounts that update as you cook
text: Your inventory knows “1 cup left”, and cooking a meal takes out what it used, with Undo.

title: Print recipe cards
text: Print 3×5, 4×6 or 5×7 cards on regular Letter paper with dashed lines to cut out.

title: Nightly backups
text: Your data is backed up every night, and you can download everything from Settings → Backups.

title: Ready to cook?
text: Recipes show what's still on your list before you start, with one tap for “I have them all”.

title: One list, sorted by store
text: Planned meals add their ingredients to one list, and TablePlan remembers which store you buy each thing at.

title: A two-week plan board
text: See the next two weeks at a glance, tap an empty day to pick a recipe, or drag meals between days.
